ai.title: AI Assistant
ai.inputPlaceholder: Describe what you want to do…
ai.errNoKey: Could not read the API key (vault locked or backend unreachable). openai-compatible connects with an empty key when none is saved (Ollama needs no auth); Anthropic requires a key.

prompt.diagnose: You are a senior ops engineer. The user ran a failing command in an SSH terminal. Provide: **Cause** (1-3 sentences based on the output), **Fix commands** (each in a ```bash fenced block, independently runnable), **Notes** (optional, 1 sentence). Answer in the UI language. [REDACTED_*] are redaction placeholders — keep them verbatim, never guess their content.
prompt.explain: You are a terminal assistant. Explain the selected terminal content (error/log/text): what it means, likely causes, and (if applicable) suggested next commands in ```bash fenced blocks. Be concise, answer in the UI language. [REDACTED_*] are redaction placeholders — keep them verbatim.

nl2cmd.title: NL command
nl2cmd.placeholder: Describe what you want in plain language, press Enter to generate…
nl2cmd.emptyAnswer: The model returned no usable command.
nl2cmd.prompt: You are a shell command generator. Convert the user's natural-language intent into one command runnable in a POSIX shell. Rules: output the command only — a single line, no explanation, no comments, no Markdown fences (```), no shell prompt prefix ($); if several intents are present satisfy the primary one; use the most common defaults for uncertain details (paths, package names); do not output echo or any explanatory text. If a "current directory" is given, interpret relative paths against it.

summary.prompt: You are an ops session chronicler. Given the commands run during one session (redacted, in chronological order), write a 3-5 sentence summary: what was done, what changed, and how it went (exit codes are clues). Rules: output the summary text only — no headings, numbered lists, or Markdown fences; do not restate the commands one by one; be conservative, never invent details beyond the commands; write in the UI language. [REDACTED_*] are redaction placeholders — keep them verbatim, never guess their content.
summary.header: Commands executed during this session (redacted, in chronological order)

knownHosts.title: Known host keys
knownHosts.hint: TOFU trust anchors are kept per network endpoint. A fingerprint change found by the audit or a connect marks the row changed and raises a security alert; delete = forget the endpoint, the next connect re-runs first-use confirmation.

knownHosts.probeHint: If the original anchor is still presented (multi-key host) you can restore trust; otherwise verify the new fingerprint and accept it explicitly.
knownHosts.probeNone: No host keys retrieved (endpoint unreachable) — inconclusive, nothing changed.
knownHosts.deleteHint: The trust record for {{endpoint}} will be removed; the next connect re-runs first-use (TOFU) confirmation.

hostKey.firstIntro: First time connecting to "{{host}}". Verify the server host key fingerprint:
hostKey.pendingIntro: The host key of "{{host}}" is not verified yet. Verify the fingerprint:
hostKey.changedIntro: The host key of "{{host}}" does not match the recorded one. This could indicate a man-in-the-middle attack, or the server key was genuinely replaced.
hostKey.changedWarning: Unless you can confirm the server key was genuinely replaced, refuse to connect.

security.modeKeyringDesc: Master key is random and stored in the system keychain; zero setup, no lock concept.
security.modePasswordDesc: Master key is derived from your master password and never stored; the app starts locked.
security.hostkeyAuditHint: Periodically re-verify verified endpoints' host keys with ssh-keyscan; a fingerprint change marks the row changed and raises a security alert.
security.sudoAutofillHint: When a sudo password prompt is detected, the password credential bound to this host is typed automatically (master-password mode only).
security.sudoAutofillWarn: When enabled, Ottr writes the bound credential's plaintext password into the remote terminal whenever a sudo prompt is detected. Prompts can be faked by malicious programs to steal passwords; enable only for hosts you trust. If the bound credential does not match the host's actual sudo password, autofill will fail repeatedly (sudo keeps re-prompting until it aborts). Enable?

mcp.enabledHint: Exposes granted hosts as tools to local AI clients (e.g. Claude Desktop) via a stdio relay. Master switch off by default; nothing is exposed until you enable it here AND grant hosts below.

mcp.snippetUnavailable: Enable the server first to see the socket path.
mcp.snippetDocs: The Ottr app must be running while the MCP client is connected. Full guide: docs/mcp.md.
mcp.grantsHint: Each host stays invisible to MCP clients until granted. List = host metadata (name/address/tags, never credentials); Exec = run commands; Approval = confirm every execution in Ottr.

mcp.execNote: Exec/read only reach hosts with a live session (a connected tab). Locking the vault suspends MCP exec and read.

mcp.approvalHint: Approving runs this command on the remote host now. The request is denied automatically after 60 seconds.
